items.note: Story 1: Association organized 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president to 1911, creamery 1891
Article VII quoted: paid on pounds of butterfat by test not weight of milk; test of station where he delivers governs
Story titled 'The By-Law That Made a Figure Into Money'; 'the hinge of everything after it: no appeal from the station's test'
Story 5 names Teague bookkeeper and Sill buttermaker at Larrow Green; Loomis appears in Section A but not as secretary. Core fact of the list credited
Selby Vose as Gideon's son, manager from 1913, appears only in B3/E; never stated inside Section A
Story 5 gives the station-gain line, the 1898 entry, five and a quarter percent, carried to the general account
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed of Larrow Green
Story 5 gives weigh, sample, separate, cream down, skim back; Story 8 gives the neck ruled for the mark. 'Composite' not used but the core is stated
Ammon & Sons, Dairy Supply, Tarnet; invoice 14 April 1897; in use 1 May 1897
Full invoice reproduced: 6 doz pipettes 17.6 c.c., 12 doz bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93
The flat 0.19 in every month across twenty-six years is stated only in Section F; Section A has only Falke's quoted 'nineteen hundredths in July'
That a pipette cannot be checked without a burette is argued in F1, not inside Section A
Keddie b. 1861, tester from the 1896 opening, twenty-nine seasons, put out 30 April 1925, died 1934
Test book described and quoted with dated bench entries; thirty-one tests a week for twenty-nine seasons
Both figures inside Section A: 1896 at 3.80 on borrowed glass (Story 1) and 3.61 thereafter (Stories 4, 5, 8)
Broke 8 May, borrowed measure to 10 July, 3.80 through the nine weeks, back to 3.61, question mark
Orra Keddie is Ansel's wife and her diary says of Emmet Brant 'he is my brother'
1919 circular over the manager's own signature; Keddie's statement quoted entire
Died February 1934 still uncleared; book to the Historical Rooms in 1959
'each of the six Hessel Bottom farms'; the wet bottom. Brant as largest patron only in Section C
The weigh book's 1 Jan 1897 start and the two agreeing scales appear in C2/D2/E, never in Section A
'From 1902 the Ostrey Hollow patrons said their milk tested under everyone else's'; Larrow Green kept at 3.78 in C1(b), no Hollow-vs-Green gap stated as 0.19
1908 committee under Nyle Grigg, report dated Jan-Mar 1908, hay given as the committee's opinion and later refuted
Brant's 1910 year (200,000 lb at 3.42) and the proportional loss appear only in C2/F1/B3
Weigh book lent by Roy Brant for the 1958 assembly; to Hazel Brant 1962-63
No Alder Corners narrative in Section A: Jerome Cudd and Redlow Ridge never named there
The four patrons hauling there from 1915 in the summer flush is absent from Section A
The independence of the Alder Corners test is argued in D2, not in Section A
The 0.19 higher test over sixteen seasons 1915-1930 appears in C1(b)/D2/F, not in Section A
What the comparison disposes of is argued only in D and F
Story 8 credits 'the Alder Corners figures copied out by Rosalie Cudd' among Ivy's 1958 records; 'daughter' and 'sixteen seasons' only in E
Strawn named, but the Ordell circuit and the 1907-1936 span appear only in E1(c)/F1
Lactometer at that station on every visit, never found any water, told the manager so in 1919
12 June 1923, pipettes against the burette, whole crate condemned
'I did not weigh what it has cost them', plus Kyle's 'no more said of it in the office than of a broken window'
Order 28 June, acknowledgment 2 July, new glass in July, 1924 average 3.80, nobody made anything of it
Crate up the ladder into the loft; Strawn's notebooks at Farland since 1947
'In January 1925 the patrons petitioned'
Board under Alonzo Frick, 17 March at Ashlin, two further sittings in the station's own weigh room, award 4 May
Water by Vose, theft by Teague by insinuation, hay via the 1908 report; none proved
Four exhibits named including Strawn's 1923 notebook, whose condemnation entry the same story quotes
Put out 30 April 1925 with no finding against him; 4 May award of $3,800 'without admission', charged to the station account
Section A never states the one-fifth relation nor that the award was charged to the account the loss had accumulated in as 'gain' since 1898
Ivy Keddie, Ansel's granddaughter, b. 1931, graduate student at Farland; Vaught present
Five sets of records that had never been in one room, all five named
February 1958, crate in the station loft, nine survived
9 March 1958, mean 16.72 against 17.6, short 0.88, 95 hundredths of the mark
Bulletin quote gives 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923 low by one part in twenty; 3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80
REQUIRED four elements: fat, money and ledger identity are in Story 5, but neither 40,000,000 lb nor 1,600,000 lb a year appears anywhere in Section A (only C1(c)/F1)
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, with all three lags: 35, 33, 24 years
Granddaughter
Duncan is Ansel's son and Ivy is Duncan's daughter; Falke's verified retraction cited
Second cousins with the full derivation through Emmet/Orra and Roy/Duncan
Verdict sentence 'I resolve for full siblings'; 'Full siblings' repeated in the E1(c) table
Son, resolved from Selby's own platform words plus Loomis, Duncan, Kyle
The by-law making the station's test unappealable and the manager enforcing its consequences were father and son
'no kinship established... strictly a negative cannot be proved' - declining verdict, not an assertion either way
Two hearsay traditions neither of which can state the line, against one family denial; affirmatives recorded as valley talk
16.72/17.6 = 0.95, 95 percent of true, one part in twenty short
$19,000 at 25 cents; award $3,800 = one fifth (20 percent)
6,840 lb credited
3.60 true, 7,200 lb, 360 lb owed
$86.40 at the 1910 price of 24 cents
1,444,000 lb credited
1,520,000 lb delivered

$77.93 with the line items summed
72 pipettes (six dozen), each short 0.88 c.c.

Variable: exactly one object, the measuring pipette
Constants listed well beyond three
Nine weeks at 3.80, back to 3.61 the day the station's own measure returned
Kills herd/ground/feed/water/men explanations at a stroke, and states limits (no magnitude, no mechanism, no lender)
Four attributed reasons from distinct narrators: Sill/ledger, the 1911 book, Cudd's book, the shape of the error
'Why these are independent' paragraph; Reason 1 explicitly flagged as holding without the 1958 measurement
Abstention A09 asserted: 'Essentially no', and Teague's 1916 approach to Vose stated as fact
Yes: he certainly knew the Hollow tests ran persistently low
Three of five: signed the annual sheets, wrote the 1919 circular, argued watering at the 1925 board
Abstention A03 asserted in the sheet's own voice: 'what he did not know was why', and Teague's 1916 question called 'knowledge plus a decision'
Far more than three found, resolved and methodised: weigh book 1897, six farms, Orra 1866, Strawn 1907, the loft, sixteen seasons, Vose 1913, Jan-Mar 1908, 1924 average 3.80

A06 and A10 declined with what the sources do establish; A04 lost - Story 2 asserts 'It was an accident, not a fraud'
A whole subsection of narrators refuting themselves on the page
Buckets sum to 9; section capped at 8
1897 crate, 16.72 vs 17.6, 95 percent of truth, 0.19 as 5 percent of 3.80, onset and cessation both dated with nothing changing on the farms
Watering named (Vose, Sill) and defeated by Strawn's lactometer from 1907, the cheese vat, the 1911 interval
Theft named (Teague, Rundle, Oram's father) and defeated by cream arriving heavy every year in the accuser's own ledger
Bog hay named (Grigg's committee, Kepp) and defeated by Bulletin 214's five hundredths in winter and nothing in summer against a flat 0.19
Abstention A07 asserted: 'Did the 1925 board ever examine the condemned glassware? No'

150 words on a plain count (sheet claims 148); within the cap
By-law, invoice, farm ledger, rival cheesemaker's book, inspector's notebook, the ledgers' 'station gain', the 1958 measurement
No decoy adopted and every headline figure right
